site.title: Generative AI — Cheat Sheets
site.tagline: Four algorithms from my handwritten GenAI-IITM.pdf notes (104 pages), a primer on the mathematics they all share, and a seven-essay course on probability that starts from counting. Each algorithm ships twice: as a self-contained interactive cheat sheet with an undergraduate-level PDF, and as an essay in the mnemonic medium with recall cards and a review deck.
site.footer: Every page is fully self-contained — no CDN, no network, works offline. Notation follows the source notes; the interactive demos are illustrative.

hero.eyebrow: IIT Madras · Mathematical Foundations of Generative AI
hero.title:
Four algorithms,
written twice each.
Seven essays beforehand.
hero.lede: Generative adversarial networks, variational autoencoders, diffusion and RLHF — pulled from 104 pages of handwritten lecture notes. Every topic ships twice: once as a self-contained interactive cheat sheet you can read in ten minutes, and once as a long-form essay in the mnemonic medium, where small recall cards inside the prose turn reading into remembering. New to the maths, or never studied probability at all? Start at the top: seven essays on probability from first principles, then the foundations primer on expectations, KL, Jensen, Gaussians and Bayes.

probability.title: Probability, from first principles
probability.sub: Seven essays in the mnemonic medium covering the ground every other page here assumes: counting, conditioning, distributions, expectation, densities, joint distributions, and the limit theorems. One chapter of Blitzstein & Hwang per essay, each with recall cards and a review deck.

site.eyebrow: IIT Madras · Mathematical Foundations of Generative AI

topics.title: Counting, and what a probability is
topics.blurb: Pebbles, sample spaces, trees, permutations, combinations, story proofs and the sieve. Chapter 1 of Blitzstein & Hwang. 4 parts, 36 recall cards.

topics.title: Conditional probability, Bayes, and being fooled by base rates
topics.blurb: Shrinking the sample space → total probability → Bayes in odds form → a rare disease in full → independence, mutual and conditional → four classic traps. Chapter 2. 36 cards.

topics.title: Random variables, and the six distributions worth knowing by name
topics.blurb: A random variable is a function → PMF and CDF → Bernoulli, Binomial, Hypergeometric, Geometric, Poisson → the categorical a language model actually emits. Chapter 3. 35 cards.

topics.title: Expectation, variance, and the bridge between them
topics.blurb: Linearity without independence → indicators and the fundamental bridge → LOTUS → variance → moments and MGFs → the square-root tax → baselines as free variance reduction. Chapters 4 and 6. 37 cards.

topics.title: Densities, bell curves, and the noise we add on purpose
topics.blurb: A density is not a probability → the normal, and why there is only one → memorylessness → universality of the uniform → reparameterization, written as μ + σε. Chapter 5. 32 cards.

topics.title: Joint distributions, the Jacobian, and conditioning on a variable
topics.blurb: Marginals, conditionals and slices → covariance, and uncorrelated-but-dependent → the multivariate normal → change of variables → the tower property that produces the ELBO. Chapters 7–9. 34 cards.

topics.title: Bounds, the law of large numbers, and the bell curve
topics.blurb: Markov, Chebyshev, Cauchy–Schwarz → Jensen, and why KL cannot be negative → LLN and CLT → error bars and the fourfold tax → MCMC when you cannot even sample. Chapter 10. 34 cards.

topics.title: The maths under generative AI, for the very curious
topics.blurb: Expectation and Monte Carlo → importance sampling → entropy, cross-entropy, KL → Jensen → Gaussian algebra → Bayes → score-function vs reparameterization. 8 parts, 57 recall cards.

topics.title: RLHF, for the very curious
topics.blurb: The same material in a mnemonic medium: story-first prose, 47 inline recall cards, an Anki-importable deck. Source pages 128–146 + the lecture.

topics.title: GANs, for the very curious
topics.blurb: f-divergence → the conjugate bound → the optimal discriminator and JS → why it saturates, in numbers → Wasserstein → cGAN, inversion → FID. 9 parts, 57 recall cards.

topics.title: VAEs, for the very curious
topics.blurb: Why the likelihood is intractable → Jensen and the exact ELBO gap → EM by hand → two gradient estimators → reparameterization → β-VAE and VQ-VAE. 8 parts, 44 recall cards.

topics.title: Diffusion, for the very curious
topics.blurb: A VAE stretched over a thousand steps → the schedule in numbers → a bound in three terms → a regression on noise → Tweedie → guidance, latent diffusion, DDIM. 9 parts, 42 recall cards.

topics.title: RLHF & Alignment
topics.blurb: MDP → policy gradient → baseline/advantage → PPO → Bradley–Terry → DPO. Source pages 128–146, merged with the lecture transcript.

topics.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
topics.blurb: f-divergence → VDM → GAN → WGAN → BiGAN → cGAN → FID. Source pages 7–42.

topics.title: Variational Auto-Encoders
topics.blurb: MLE → Jensen → ELBO → EM/GMM → reparameterization → β-VAE → VQ-VAE. Source pages 43–71.

topics.title: Diffusion Models
topics.blurb: DDPM → ELBO → denoising → U-Net → score → guidance → LDM → DDIM. Source pages 72–110.
